PUSHYABHUTI/VARDHANA DYNASTY

  • Founder: Pushyabhuti
  • They were ruling in Thaneshwar (now in Haryana).
  • Son: Prabhakaravardhana

Prabhakaravardhana had two sons and a daughter:

  • Rajyavardhana (eldest)
  • Harshavardhana (youngest)
  • Rajyashri (daughter) who married Grahavarman (he was a member of the Maukhari Dynasty, ruling at Kannauj)

Grahavarman was killed by the combined armies of Devgupta (Ruler of Malwa) and Shashanka (Ruler of Gauda). Subsequently, Rajyavardhana was also killed. Harshvardhana took revenge by defeating the Gauda King Shashanka.

Harshavardhana (606 AD-647 AD)

  • Capital: Kannauj
  • Defeated: Dhruvasena II (ruler of Maitraka Dynasty and then married his daughter to him to secure the western boundary).
  • Visited by traveller: Hiuen-Tsang (Xuang-Zang) → 2nd Chinese traveller.
  • Book by Hiuen Tsang → Si-yu-ki: Records of the Western World.
  • He was a shaivite and patronised Buddhist religion.
  • He authored 3 books: Ratnavali, Nagananda, and Priyadarshika.
  • Biography of Harshavardhana "Harshacharitra" written by his court poet Banabhatta (he also wrote: Kadambari).
  • He was defeated by Pulakeshin II (Chalukyan king) on the banks of Narmada river.
  • His administrative empire was divided into two parts: directly administered territories and feudatory states.

Map 1: Post-Gupta Period (625 AD)

Maukhari Dynasty: Ishanavarman, an important ruler of Maukhari Dynasty took title of Maharajadhiraja.

CHALUKYA DYNASTY

  • Chalukya Dynasty rulers were feudatories of Kadambas of Banavasi.
  • They were divided into three distinct dynasties:
  • Badami Chalukya (Early Chalukya) → Capital: Vatapi
  • Eastern Chalukya → Capital: Vengi
  • Western Chalukya (Later Chalukya) → Capital: Kalyani

BADAMI CHALUKYA

Jayasimha

  • He was the founder this dynasty.
  • Capital: Vatapi

Pulakeshin I (543 AD-566 AD)

  • He was the founder of Badami Chalukya Dynasty.
  • Pulakeshin I had two son: Kirtivarman I and Mangalesha (Mangalesh was killed by Kirtivarman I's son Pulakeshin II, who later ascended the throne).

Pulakeshin II (610 AD-642 AD)

  • He is considered the greatest ruler of this dynasty.
  • After defeating Harshavardhana, Pulakeshin II took the title of "Dakshinapatheshwara" (Lord of South).
  • Other title taken by him: Parameshwar
  • He also defeated Mahendravarman I (Pallava ruler) in the Battle of Pullalur.
  • He was defeated by Narasimhavarman I (son of Mahendravarman I), who later took the title of "Vatapikonda" (Conquerer of Vatapi) after defeating Pulakeshin II.
  • Aihole Pillar Inscription (Karnataka) was about Pulakeshin II, composed by his court poet Ravikirti.

Vikramaditya I

  • He was the third son of Pulakeshin II.
  • His great grandson Kirtivarman II (last ruler of Badami Chalukya) was defeated by Dantidurga who later founded Rashtrakuta Dynasty.

Chalukyan Architecture

  • Chalukyas built temples at Aihole and Pattadakal. They introduced a new temple architecture called Vesara Style (covered in next chapter).

Aihole

Pattadakal

  • Built by: Queen Lokamaha devi (she married Chalukyan King → Vikramaditya II)
  • Dedicated to: Lord Shiva
  • Built in: Dravida style
  • A total of 10 temples seen here: 4 (Nagara style) and 6 (Dravida style)
  • Declared as UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987.
  • Pattadakal group of temples are known as "Cradle of Indian Architecture".
  • Built in: Dravida style
  • Dedicated to: Lord Shiva
  • Built in: Nagara style
  • Built by: Narasimhavarman I
  • These temples are also known as Pancha Rathas or Pandava Rathas

PALLAVA DYNASTY (575 AD-897 AD)

  • Founder: Simha Vishnu
  • Capital: Kanchipuram
  • Pallavas were feudatories to Kalabhras.
  • Greatest ruler: Mahendravarman I
  • Son: Narasimhavarman I (Ruling period: 630 AD-668 AD) (Title taken: Mahamalla).
  • Narasimhavarman I also founded the port city Mahabalipuram.
  • They developed the Dravida architecture temples.

Pallava Architecture

  • Added to UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1984.
  • Built by: Narasimhavarman II
  • Dedicated to: Lord Shiva
  • Built by: Narasimhavarman II

RASHTRAKUTA DYNASTY (755 AD-878 AD)

  • Founder: Dantidurga (he established the dynasty by overthrowing the Chalukyas of Badami).
  • Capital: Manyakheta
  • Dantidurga performed 'Hiranyagarbha' (golden womb).

Krishna I (756 AD-774 AD)

  • Son of Dantidurga.
  • He built Kailasha Temple of Ellora (this temple is a Monolithic Stone Temple (built with a single rock)).
  • Aurangzeb, the Mughal Emperor, once attempted to destroy the temple.

Govinda III (793 AD-814 AD)

  • He defeated Pratihara king Nagabhatta II.

Amoghavarsha (814 AD-878 AD)

  • He was converted to Jainism.
  • Books written by him: Kavirajamarga, Prashnottara Ratnamalika.

Krishna III (939 AD-967 AD)

  • He defeated the Cholas.

Architecture

  • Ellora Caves (Aurangabad, Maharashtra) showcase temples of Hindu, Jain, and Buddhist architecture which were primarily built by the Rashtrakutas with contribution from Chalukyas and Yadavas.
  • Dedicated to: Lord Vishnu

HOYSALA DYNASTY

  • They were feudatory to Chalukyas of Kalyani (Later Chalukyas)
  • Capital: Dwarasamudra (Halebidu)
  • Founder: Nripa Kama II

Architecture

  • Star-shaped temple.
  • Built by: King Vishnuvardhana.
  • Style of architecture: Bhumija style of architecture.
  • Dedicated to: Lord Vishnu
  • 42nd UNESCO World Heritage Site
  • Dedicated to: Lord Shiva
  • 3 Jain Basadis are within the complex.

Important Battles

  • Pulakeshin II defeated Harshavardhana
  • Pulakeshin II defeated Mahendravarman I
  • Narasimhavarman I defeated Pulakeshin II
